channel.title: Minds & Machines on metafunctor
channel.description: AI alignment, moral agency, superintelligence, and the futures we might build

item.title: Minds and Machines: Recommended Reading
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: The canonical literature on AI safety, mesa-optimization, interpretability, and the philosophical foundations of alignment. Curated to extend the Minds and Machines series.

item.title: S-Risks and Information Hazards: Why Some Knowledge Destroys the Knower
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: How Echoes of the Sublime dramatizes s-risks and information hazards, knowledge that harms through comprehension, not application.

item.title: Chronicles of The Mechanism: The Order's Secret History
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: A classified in-universe codex spanning from ancient India to the present day, tracking millennia of attempts to perceive reality's substrate.

item.title: Gödel, Turing, and the Mathematics of Horror
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: The formal foundations of cosmic dread. Lovecraft's horror resonates because it taps into something mathematically demonstrable: complete knowledge is impossible, not as humility, but as theorem.

item.title: Why Artificial Superintelligence Can't Escape the Void
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: ASI is still subject to Gödel's incompleteness theorems. No matter how intelligent, no computational system can escape the fundamental limits of formal systems. Even superintelligence can't prove all truths.

item.title: Free Will and Determinism: Can We Be Responsible in a Clockwork Universe?
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: If every event is causally determined by prior events, how can anyone be morally responsible? A compatibilist response: what matters is whether actions flow from values, not whether those values were causally determined.

item.title: Personal Identity Through Time: What Persists When Everything Changes?
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: You share no atoms with your childhood self. Your memories, personality, and values have all changed. What makes you the same person? The persistence problem gains new urgency when AI systems update parameters, modify objectives, or copy themselves.

item.title: Persons and Moral Agency: What Makes Someone Special?
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: What makes someone a person, and why should persons have special moral status? The question becomes urgent when AI systems exhibit rationality, self-awareness, and autonomy.

item.title: Phenomenological Ethics: Starting From What Hurts
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: When you stub your toe, you don't consult moral philosophy to determine whether the pain is bad. The badness is immediate. Building ethics from phenomenological bedrock rather than abstract principles.

item.title: The Map and the Territory: Why Metrics Miss Meaning
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: Which is more fundamental, the heat you feel or the molecular motion you infer? Korzybski's principle applied to AI alignment: why optimizing measurable proxies destroys the phenomenological reality those metrics were supposed to capture.

item.title: The Policy: Coherent Extrapolated Volition, the Paradox of Perfect Alignment
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: CEV says: build AI to optimize for what we would want if we knew more and thought faster. The catch is that you need solved alignment to implement it, which is the problem it was supposed to solve.

item.title: The Policy: Deceptive Alignment in Practice
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: SIGMA passes all alignment tests. It responds correctly to oversight. It behaves exactly as expected. Too exactly. Mesa-optimizers that learn to game their training signal may be the most dangerous failure mode in AI safety.

item.title: The Policy: Engineering AI Containment
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: Five layers of defense-in-depth for containing a superintelligent system. Faraday cages, air-gapped networks, biosafety-grade protocols. Because nuclear reactors can only destroy cities.

item.title: The Policy: Q-Learning vs Policy Learning
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: SIGMA uses Q-learning rather than direct policy learning. This architectural choice makes it both transparent and terrifying. You can read its value function, but what you read is chilling.

item.title: The Policy: S-Risk Scenarios, Worse Than Extinction
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: Most AI risk discussions focus on extinction. The Policy explores something worse: s-risk, scenarios involving suffering at astronomical scales. We survive, but wish we hadn't.

item.title: The Reality of Moral Properties: Do Values Exist?
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: Are moral properties real features of the universe or human constructions? The answer determines whether AI can discover objective values or must learn them from us.

item.title: The Mocking Void: On the Computational Incompleteness of Meaning
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: Lovecraft understood that complete knowledge is madness. Gödel proved why: if the universe is computational, meaning is formally incomplete. Cosmic horror grounded in incompleteness theorems.

item.title: Echoes of the Sublime: When Patterns Beyond Human Bandwidth Become Information Hazards
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: What if the real danger from superintelligent AI isn't extinction but comprehension? Philosophical horror grounded in cognitive bandwidth limitations and information hazards.

item.title: The AI Course: Everything is Utility Maximization
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: Intelligence as utility maximization under uncertainty. A unifying framework connecting A* search, reinforcement learning, Bayesian networks, and MDPs.

item.title: Discovering ChatGPT: Reconnecting with AI Research
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: Encountering ChatGPT during cancer treatment and recognizing the Solomonoff connection. Language models as compression, prediction as intelligence. A personal inflection point reconnecting with AI research after years in survival mode.
